system.help.backup.title: Backup
system.help.backup.intro: From here you can create a console tar.gz together with a separate Pad database backup, save code with commit/push, and restore the console from disk or GitHub. It also gathers maintenance restarts; the entire tab is admin-only.
system.help.backup.first.title: Getting started
system.help.backup.first.step1: Select Create backup now and wait for it to appear in the list.
system.help.backup.first.step2: To back up code, review the remote, branch, exclusions, and new files.
system.help.backup.first.step3: Choose Commit without push to save locally, or Push to send to the personal remote.
system.help.backup.first.step4: Use Restore or Pull only after reading the confirmation and understanding which state will change.
system.help.backup.first.step5: Under Maintenance, choose Restart sessions or Restart server depending on what needs refreshing.
system.help.backup.buttons.title: Buttons and actions
system.help.backup.buttons.create.v: Creates a console tar.gz and, best-effort, a separate Pad .db. The latest backups of each type are kept. Admin-only.
system.help.backup.buttons.restore.v: Overwrites the current state with that tar.gz and restarts the web app. Destructive and admin-only.
system.help.backup.buttons.delete.v: Permanently deletes that backup file after confirmation. Admin-only.
system.help.backup.buttons.commit.v: Creates a local commit with the selected changes; it does not touch GitHub. Admin-only.
system.help.backup.buttons.generate.v: Suggests an editable commit message with a short Haiku run. CONSUMES TOKENS and is admin-only.
system.help.backup.buttons.push.v: Commits and pushes only to the allowed personal remote; every new file requires human selection. Admin-only.
system.help.backup.buttons.pull.v: Runs fetch + fast-forward and protects local changes with a stash; installs dependencies if needed and restarts only with a healthy tree. Admin-only.
system.help.backup.buttons.sessions.v: Sends SIGTERM to live chat runners. It does not touch the service, loses no history, and relaunches them with --resume. Admin-only.
system.help.backup.buttons.server.v: Restarts the web process; tmux and runners survive, and the page waits for it to return. Admin-only.
system.help.backup.warning.title: Watch out
system.help.backup.warning.text: Restore and Delete act on the console tar.gz; the Pad .db is kept as a separate backup and cannot be restored from this panel. Push is blocked outside the personal remote and never includes .env, users.json, or certs; untracked files never travel without your checkmark. Restarting sessions is not the same as restarting the server.

system.sponsorship.help.first.step3: Open Waiting for a sponsor and check the person's name.
system.sponsorship.help.first.step4: Select Sponsor and confirm that you accept paying for their usage with your credential.

system.sponsorship.help.title: Sponsorship
system.sponsorship.help.warning.text: The token comes from YOUR Claude subscription: anyone you sponsor uses your account, and you pay for their turns. Generating the token is only a login and does not consume AI tokens. If you release the person, they immediately lose the ability to work. A sponsored account cannot sponsor another person.
system.sponsorship.help.warning.title: Watch out
system.sponsorship.help.what.text: The sponsorship token is a dedicated claude setup-token credential that the console lends to people you sponsor. Without it, the person exists but cannot work. When you sponsor them, their usage is charged to your subscription until you release them.
system.sponsorship.help.what.title: What it is
